html:
Kilwa was a Swahili city-state on an island off the south coast of Tanzania, which at its height in the 13th to 15th centuries was the strongest town on the East African coast.

Its rulers claimed descent from a Persian prince of Shiraz. By taking control of Sofala, they took the gold trade from Great Zimbabwe. They minted copper coins and built the Great Mosque and the palace of Husuni Kubwa. Ibn Battuta visited in 1331 and called it one of the most beautiful cities in the world.

The Portuguese sacked it in 1505 and built a fort there, and it never regained its wealth. The ruins of Kilwa Kisiwani were listed by UNESCO in 1981, among the most important of the Swahili city-states.
sum: Kilwa was a Swahili city-state on an island off the south coast of Tanzania, which at its height in the 13th to 15th centuries was the strongest town on the East African coast.
